conviction_note: The evidence balances out. The Q2 report's own inventory build 'ahead of planned Q3 deliveries' and the Transsion IPR settlement support the quarter. The pressure from memory-component costs, which TrendForce expects to keep rising in 4Q26, weighs on the Q4 Networks margin guide, and that guide is what the stock traded on in July. So p_up is 50 and abs_move is 10, set above the 8.6% implied move because confirmed prints have moved this name 8-20% (Q3'25 roughly +12-20%, Q2'26 -8 to -13.5%) and this is the new CEO's first report. The findings sum to -0.2, which is consistent with a scaled 0.
bar: Infront consensus compiled 2026-10-08 from 16 analysts: net sales SEK 55.4bn, Networks SEK 35.1bn (+6% QoQ), CSS SEK 15.2bn, adj. gross margin 47.3%, adj. EBITA SEK 7.9bn / 14.2% (https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/, 2026-10-12). The company's own 2026-07-27 Infront PDF agrees: sales 55,531m, EBITA 7,945m, GM 47.3% (https://www.ericsson.com/4a1f6a/assets/local/investors/documents/shareholder-information/analyst-consensus/eric-post-26q2-web-consensus---infront.pdf; the PDF now returns 404, figures via search snippet). Company guide: Networks Q3 sales above the +1% three-year seasonality, CSS in line with +3%, Networks adj. GM 48-50% (https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points, 2026-09-11). Two agreeing estimate sources plus a company guide, so the bar is sourced.
positioning_check: ADR short interest about 70.1M shares as of 2026-08-19, up about 5.9M, 4.6 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/eric/shortinterest). That is roughly 2% of about 3.37bn shares, so the short is not crowded. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline, so there is no directional statement. Put/call OI is 0.31, call-heavy. Spot $9.665 is 5.6% above the 52-week low and 29.7% below the high. 20-day run-up -3.6%, 5-day +2.2%.

findings.finding: Ericsson's own Q2 report says operating cash flow fell 'mainly due to higher inventories ahead of planned Q3 deliveries' (SEK -4.4bn change in operating net assets), and the CEO expects 'higher volumes of network rollout projects' in Q3. That backs Networks sales clearing the +6% QoQ consensus (SEK 35.1bn vs Q2 SEK 33.0bn).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26: sales missed (SEK 52.7bn vs about 53.9bn Bloomberg) and the stock fell 8-13.5%, but the cut to the margin guide was named as the driver (https://www.rttnews.com/3666700/ericsson-stock-drops-on-weak-q2-cautious-view-on-q3-networks-margin.aspx). Q3'25: a beat across the board went with a +12-20% day (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/10/14/why-ericsson-stock-jumped-to-multiyear-highs-today).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Consensus already sits at +6% QoQ, well above the company's '+1% seasonality' floor, and the Hurbra preview frames sales as merely seasonal. If the market had fully read the inventory line, consensus would be above 6% and not have drifted down from SEK 55.5bn to 55.4bn between July and October. The finding lands inside what the company guided to, so it is kept small.
findings.independence: Vodafone Idea's deployment over two quarters (finding 4) is a separate counterparty pointing the same way. It shares no document with this one.

findings.finding: The Transsion global settlement and licence of 2026-07-08 is 'expected to be reflected beginning in Q3 2026'. IPR run-rate after the July deals is SEK 13.5bn a year (about 3.4bn a quarter) against Q1's 3.1bn, and any catch-up for Transsion's unlicensed period would be booked in Q3 at roughly 100% gross margin, 82% of it in Networks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 organic sales fell 1% 'primarily due to lower IPR licensing revenues' after a one-off partial settlement in Q2'25 (SEK 3.4bn vs 4.9bn), so IPR swings have moved headline numbers before. No clean isolated reaction to an IPR line is available.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The Hurbra preview says licensing incl. Transsion is expected to lift Q3, and the run-rate is public. A catch-up amount was never disclosed, so consensus can only carry a guess. If it were fully modelled, group GM consensus would not sit at 47.3%, about 1.1pt below Q2's 48.4%, when a high-margin IPR step-up lands in the quarter. Sized small because the catch-up part is a one-off with no path to the guide.
findings.independence: Run-rate figure from the Q2 report's key data points page (https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points), which is a company document separate from the settlement release.

findings.finding: TrendForce forecast (2026-09-30) has conventional DRAM contract prices rising another 10-15% QoQ in 4Q26 after 13-18% in 3Q26. Ericsson said in July that the component-cost hit will 'build up in the second half of this and into next year', so the Q4 Networks gross-margin guide is more likely than not to show continued pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26: the Q3 Networks GM guide of 48-50% (vs 50.4% in Q2) with the component-cost warning produced the worst earnings-day reaction in about three years, -8% to -13.5% (https://www.insidermonkey.com/blog/why-ericssons-worst-day-in-three-years-wasnt-about-this-quarters-numbers-1803484/).
findings.why_not_priced: The cost direction is public and the stock is down about 30% from its high, so most of it is in the price. What is not visible is the size of the Q4 guide. If the market expected a further step down, the 52-week low (5.6% below spot) would already have been broken and consensus EBITA would have kept falling. Instead it has been stable at about SEK 7.9bn since July. Offsetting this, Ericsson said renegotiated contract prices would become 'gradually visible', which caps the size.
findings.independence: Ericsson's own Q2 call comment, 'build up in the second half ... into next year' (https://www.lightreading.com/finance/ericsson-warns-of-price-rises-to-counter-high-component-costs, 2026-07-14). Macro-to-company transmission: the size of the Q4 effect is a proxy and unconfirmed.

findings.finding: Vodafone Idea said on 2026-08-11 it has placed about ₹9,000 crore of equipment orders with Ericsson, Nokia and Samsung, to be deployed 'over the next two quarters' (Aug 2026 to Jan 2027). That supports Ericsson's India Networks deliveries in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Unavailable. India is a sub-line of market area SEA/Oceania/India (SEK 5.4bn in Q2) and has not been an isolated mover on prior prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a counterparty statement made after Ericsson last spoke (2026-07-14), but it is split across three vendors and is small against SEK 35bn of Networks sales. Net of the rest of the company, it is a fraction of a point.
findings.independence: A different source from finding 1 pointing the same way on Q3 Networks volumes.

findings.finding: Per Narvinger became CEO on 2026-10-01 and presents his first report two weeks later. 2026 restructuring is already guided 'elevated' (FY26 consensus SEK -5.5bn), so a new-CEO reset of targets or charges is a live possibility on this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CEO-transition print in the window. Narvinger ran Business Area Networks from March 2025, so this is an internal successor and continuity is the base case.
findings.why_not_priced: The appointment is fully known. What is not known is whether the first report resets anything. The sign is ambiguous: a cost programme could be bought, a lower margin ambition sold. Sized near zero, and the effect goes mostly into abs_move_pct.

outside_window.finding: Nokia's Q3 2026 report (tentatively 2026-10-22) is the first peer read on Q3 RAN demand and memory-cost pass-through. Nokia guided Q3 sales +3-7% QoQ on 2026-07-23.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (null). Near-balanced findings on a stock 5.6% off its 52-week low and down 30% from its high are consistent with a market that already holds the margin worry, so nothing here cuts hard against the tape.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, inside the guide: the inventory and Q3 deliveries finding lands inside the company's 'above seasonality' guide, and consensus is already at +6%. 0.8 -> 0.4.
Rule 2, one-offs: the Transsion catch-up part is a below-the-line-like one-off with no path to the guide. 0.8 -> 0.4.

Rule 5, proxy: the memory-cost size for the Q4 guide is macro-to-company transmission. Direction is company-confirmed, magnitude is not. -1.2 -> -0.9. Rule 7: short interest checked (4.6 days, about 2% of shares, not crowded), so no further shrink.
Rules 5 and 9: the Vodafone Idea order is split three ways and small net of the rest of Networks. 0.3 -> 0.2.
Last section of the lessons file, untrustworthy history: rebuilt the base rate from confirmed prints (Q3'25 +12-20%, Q2'26 -8 to -13.5%). abs_move 9.5 -> 10.0.
Rule 3, read the set: with the findings now near zero net, p_up goes from 52 to 50 and the scaled move to 0.
